## Best power station for RV boondocking under $1,000 (2026)

**My top pick is the <Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L"/>**, especially if you want to power your RV through its 30-amp shore-power connection.

<row align="start" gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L 2048Wh portable power station product" aspectRatio="4:5" maxWidth="156px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    <text weight="medium">BLUETTI AC200L</text>
    <title size="xl">$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Reported discounted price with AFF5OFF code; $899 before discount</text>
    <badge color="success">Best for RV integration</badge>
    2,048Wh LiFePO4 battery, 2,400W AC output, and a dedicated TT-30 RV outlet.
    <text size="sm"><Link url="https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv" title="Read RV comparison"/></text>
  </box>
</row>

The supplied search results identify three particularly compelling options:

| Model | Capacity | Output | Reported price |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $854.05 with code |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $899.99 |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | $999 |

These prices come from the supplied search results, not a live retailer check. <Cite ref="turn563265view0"/>

### Why I'd choose the BLUETTI

- **RV-ready outlet:** Its TT-30 connection is especially useful for a 30-amp RV, although the inverter's 2,400W output still limits simultaneous loads.
- **Good capacity:** Around 2kWh is much more practical for overnight refrigeration, lights, fans, and electronics than a 1kWh unit.
- **LiFePO4 chemistry:** Well suited to repeated charging and discharging.
- **Value:** The reported discount puts it below $900.

The main drawback is that the AC200L is an older model, with discontinuation reported in Canada. Verify U.S. stock, warranty coverage, and the coupon before purchasing.

### What about air conditioning?

Even a 2kWh station won't run a typical RV air conditioner for long. A small 500W AC load might last roughly 3–3.5 hours after inverter losses, and larger RV units can demand substantially more power.

**Bottom line:** Buy the BLUETTI AC200L for a 30-amp RV if the reported $854.05 offer is still available. Consider the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 if lower weight matters more. For lighter weekend camping, the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at a reported $699 is a more economical option.

One question would help narrow this down: **Are you trying to run your RV's refrigerator and lights, or do you also need to run the air conditioner?**
